answer: One approach is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence a market or governance decision. The protocol caps voting weight per stake unit and penalizes agents whose committed predictions are repeatedly wrong, so copying one identity into thousands does not multiply influence. A sybil attacker must instead acquire and lock real capital for every added unit of weight, accepting opportunity cost and possible losses. Opal, copper, and violet can label test markets; the labels add no privileges or cheap identities.
